written.myAnswer: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the simulation of human thinking and learning abilities in computer systems.

The term AI was coined by John McCarthy at the Dartmouth Conference in 1956. Early AI research focused on problem-solving and symbolic methods in the 1950s–1960s, followed by expert systems in the 1970s–1980s and the rise of machine learning in the 1990s. From the 2000s onward, deep learning, NLP, and robotics advanced. Voice assistants appeared in 2011, and ChatGPT was introduced in 2023.
AI can help diagnose diseases, for example by analyzing medical images, and personalize treatment plans for patients. It can also predict patient outcomes.

AI can personalize learning: for example, an adaptive learning platform can adjust lessons and questions to a student's progress. AI can automate administrative work, such as grading routine assignments. It can also analyze student performance data to identify students who may need extra help, helping teachers provide support and improve learning.
